The Iron Rule of the Matching Card
The lone card commands over the pile: absolute priority on single matching cards.
A single matching card always takes absolute precedence over any sum on the table.

Cards, Coins, Settebello, and Primiera: how a hand is decided.
Each deal awards 4 basic points: Cards (21+), Coins (6+), Settebello, and Primiera.

At least 6 cards out of 10 (absolute majority)
Perfect! 6 coins out of 10 mathematically guarantees the point.

If no single matching card exists, always select the combination holding Coins or high Primiera cards.

First Chapter completed with honor! You now possess the club fundamentals.
The Hidden Mathematics of the 4 Suits
Discover the Renaissance scoring scale (7=21, 6=18), the empty suit trap, and rapid counting.
In Primiera face cards are weak: discover the true rulers of the deck.
In Primiera Face cards are worth only 10 points; Sevens equal 21 and Sixes equal 18.
Many think face cards are worth a lot. In Primiera the scale is inverted: 7 is 21, 6 is 18, Ace is 16. How much is a King worth in Primiera?
Only 10 points, even less than a Two (12 pt)
Exactly! Kings and Jacks are only worth 10 points. The true rulers of Primiera are Sevens and Sixes!
20 points, because it is the highest card in the deck
No! Don\'t let the crown fool you: all face cards are only worth 10 points in Primiera!
Great! Never sacrifice a 6 or 7 to save a face card in Primiera.
Primiera sums the top card of each suit: leave no empty holes.
Primiera is calculated by summing the best card per suit: Swords + Cups + Coins + Clubs.
How is the Primiera score calculated at the end of the deal?
By summing the highest card for each of the 4 suits
Exactly! Without a card in every suit you can\'t win Primiera.
By summing all captured cards of rank 7
Wrong: Sevens are valuable, but if a suit is missing, their value is wasted!
Golden rule: a Primiera with all 4 suits covered is an impregnable fortress.
Why three 7s and zero Clubs loses Primiera against modest cards.
Without at least one card in every suit you can\'t win Primiera: sevens alone won\'t save you!
You already captured three Sevens (Swords, Cups, and Coins), but zero Clubs! On the table lies the 5 of Clubs. Capture it immediately with your 5 of Swords to cover the fourth suit!
Well done! With the 5 of Clubs you locked Primiera at 78 points and avoided defeat!
Learn to calculate winning scores at a glance (84, 81, 78 pt).
With 4 suits covered, 3 Sevens and a Six score 81 points and are almost unbeatable.
Both players have covered all 4 suits. You captured 3 Sevens and a Six (81 pt). Your opponent has 1 Seven and three Sixes (75 pt). Who wins Primiera?
You win: 81 points against your opponent\'s 75 points
Flawless mathematics! Whoever has more Sevens with all suits covered dominates the count.
It\'s a tie because both have high cards
No: Primiera is calculated by summing the exact values of each suit (81 to 75)!
Second Chapter mastered! You now command the deepest secrets of Primiera.
Learn the critical threshold of 10, how to fortify the board against Sweeps, and the dealer\'s endgame.
No single card equals 11 or higher: a sum above 10 is completely safe.
If the total sum of board cards exceeds 10, no single card can make a Sweep.

The King: raising the sum to 14 makes a single-card Sweep impossible
Hats off! No single card equals 14: when the sum exceeds 10, the board is completely safe!
The 3: it\'s a lower card and less appealing to the opponent
Danger! With 4+3=7 any opponent holding a 7 lands an immediate Sweep and cleans the board!
Fundamental rule: always exceed 10 when you have no captures available.

Creating sums that the opponent cannot combine with remaining cards.
In defensive drops sacrifice lost neutral suits, protecting Coins and Primiera suits.

False! On the very last play of the deal a Sweep never counts, even if you clear the table.

Every missed capture tells you what the opponent does not possess.
